title: The client that grew them into a loss
units_note: All money figures in ₹ lakh unless marked. Costs are shown in brackets, e.g. (234). Shipments are in lakh parcels.

brief.tag: Case file · Swift Parcel · Delhi NCR
brief.headline: Shipments up 30%. A ₹18L profit became a ₹16L loss.
brief.story: Swift Parcel is a courier aggregator: it picks up parcels from online sellers and hands them to national carriers, charging sellers a per-parcel rate and paying carriers for each parcel they move. In July it signed Bazaarly, a fast-growing marketplace, and volume jumped 30%. The quarter ended in a loss anyway. The founder thinks the carriers are overcharging and wants to start a fight with them.

body.text: Gross margin (revenue minus carrier costs) fell from 22% to 9%.
70% of Bazaarly parcels go to metro pin codes, the same mix as existing sellers.

Existing sellers are billed on the weight the carrier measures. Bazaarly's contract bills on the weight its sellers declare at booking, a condition Bazaarly asked for before signing. Bazaarly pays the standard rate card, with no extra discount.

rows: Existing sellers: carrier cost per parcel
Bazaarly: average weight measured by carrier

body.text: Carriers bill on the higher of actual weight and volumetric (box size) weight, measured by scanners at their hubs. Return-to-origin charges are included in these per-parcel costs.
Carriers attach scanner photos to each rejected dispute. Most show Bazaarly parcels in oversized boxes with air pillows.
Already included in the carrier cost per parcel.

evidence.teaser: How the Bazaarly deal was won

body.text: “Signed Bazaarly! 2 lakh parcels a quarter. They insisted on declared-weight billing, which everyone in the market is offering now. Small price for the biggest deal of the year.”
Sales commission: 2% of revenue, about ₹1.3L on Bazaarly in Q2.

causes.label: Carrier fuel surcharges went up
causes.feedback: Fuel moved from 12% to 13% of the base rate, about ₹2L. Existing sellers' cost per parcel didn't change at all.

causes.label: Carriers are overcharging on weight
causes.feedback: Swift lost 96% of its weight disputes, and the scanner photos show bulky boxes. The parcels really do weigh 1.5 kg.

causes.label: More parcels are being returned to sellers
causes.feedback: Bazaarly's return rate is higher, but return charges are already inside the ₹48 per parcel, worth a couple of lakh at most.

causes.label: The new client is billed on declared weight but carriers charge real weight, so every one of its parcels loses money
Existing sellers negotiated lower rates
causes.feedback: Existing revenue per parcel held at ₹50, and their margin barely moved.

causes.label: Existing sellers are leaving
causes.feedback: Existing parcels dipped 3% and revenue fell ₹10L, but their gross margin only fell about ₹2L.

causes.label: Staff costs went up
causes.feedback: Staff costs were ₹30L in both quarters.

causes.label: Cash-on-delivery money is stuck
causes.feedback: More COD cash is held, but that's a cash timing issue, not a loss.

causes.label: Bazaarly is paying late
causes.feedback: Bazaarly pays within 15 days, with nothing overdue.

causes.label: Bazaarly got too big a volume discount
causes.feedback: Bazaarly pays the standard rate card, with no extra discount. The problem is which weight the rate is applied to.

bonus.question: If Swift moves Bazaarly to carrier-measured weight on the standard rate card, and volume and weights stay the same, what happens to its quarterly gross profit on Bazaarly?
options: It turns positive, to about +₹20L a quarter
It can't be estimated without fuel prices
bonus.explanation: A 1.5 kg parcel falls in the 1–2 kg slab, billed at ₹58. It costs ₹48 to ship, so Swift earns about ₹10 a parcel instead of losing ₹16. On 2 lakh parcels that's about +₹20L a quarter, turning the ₹32L loss into a profit, before any volume Bazaarly might move elsewhere.

explanation.answer: Bazaarly is billed on the weight its sellers declare (0.5 kg, ₹32 a parcel), but carriers charge Swift on the weight their scanners measure (1.5 kg, ₹48 a parcel). Each of Bazaarly's 2 lakh parcels loses ₹16, about ₹32L for the quarter. That's 94% of the ₹34L swing from profit to loss.
fastest_path: Open the P&L. Carrier costs jumped far faster than revenue; gross margin fell from 22% to 9%.
Open revenue by client. All the growth is Bazaarly: ₹64L of revenue.
Open carrier invoices. Bazaarly parcels cost ₹48 each and weigh 1.5 kg; 2 lakh of them cost ₹96L against ₹64L billed.
Open rate card & contracts. Bazaarly is billed on declared weight, so a 1.5 kg parcel is charged as 0.5 kg.
traps: "Carriers are overcharging" is what the founder believes. The dispute log shows the carriers are right.
Fuel surcharges and returns both rose, but both are small and already priced into the per-parcel costs.
"Too big a volume discount" is the near-miss: the rate is standard. It's applied to the wrong weight.
explanation.lesson: Volume you lose money on isn't growth. It's a faster way to shrink.
